newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian ministers leave for Iraqi oil talks.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian ministers leave for Iraqi oil talks.

text.p: Jordan's ministers of trade and energy left for Baghdad on Wednesday to try to clinch an accord holding up an oil deal supplying the kingdom's energy needs for 1997, officials said.

Jordanian officials said they were hopeful the visit by Minister of Trade Ali Abu al-Ragheb and Energy Minister Hashem Dabbas would settle a dispute which surfaced when Iraq asked for higher prices for the oil it barters for Jordanian goods.

Jordan is supplied under an annual trade protocol with most of its energy needs -- around 75,000 bpd of crude oil and petroleum products -- at concessionary terms in a deal exempt from the strict U.N. embargo slapped on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Jordan said it halved the value of goods sent to Iraq last year to $220 million because it said Iraq was accruing heavy debts under the previous accords.
This year Jordan is also seeking a seven percent increase in Iraqi oil supplies, Dabbas said earlier this month.
Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz said on Monday his country was committed to supplying Jordan with oil, but queried Jordan's debt claim.
Jordanian businessmen, who are paid by Jordan's Central Bank for goods sent to Iraq under the protocol, have called for an increase in its volume this year.
